title: The deficit that would not shrink
hook: Tariffs were meant to close America's trade gap. The deficit with China shrank, but the overall gap barely moved: it shifted to Vietnam, Taiwan and Mexico.
notes: All figures: US Census Bureau, US goods trade by partner country (exports minus general imports, Census basis, not seasonally adjusted), FT-900 country file with data through August 2026; goods only, services are not included. '12 months' means the 12 months ending in the month shown; December values are calendar years. A negative balance is a US deficit. Gold: US Census Bureau and BEA, 'U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, August 2026' (6 October 2026): exports of nonmonetary gold were $86.6 billion in January-August 2026 against $40.1 billion a year earlier. Hong Kong is counted separately from mainland China. Bilateral balances are partly an artefact of where goods are finished: goods assembled in Vietnam or Mexico from Chinese parts count as Vietnamese or Mexican imports. The saving-investment link is an accounting identity of national accounts: a country's current-account balance equals its saving minus its investment.

scenes.title: A record gap
scenes.text: In 2024 the US bought $1.2 trillion more goods from the rest of the world than it sold. In 2025, when tariffs rose to their highest level since the 1940s, the gap grew to a record $1.23 trillion. In 1990 it was about $100 billion.

scenes.title: Who the US buys more from
scenes.text: In 2024 the biggest gap was with China: the US bought $297 billion more from China than it sold there. Mexico ($169 billion), Vietnam ($123 billion), Ireland and Germany followed. Blue marks a US deficit. The US sold more than it bought to the Netherlands, Hong Kong, the UAE and Australia.

layers.title: US goods trade balance, 2024 (blue: US deficit)

scenes.title: The gap moves
scenes.text: In the 12 months to August 2026 the deficit with China was down to $166 billion, the smallest since 2004. Now Vietnam ($229 billion), Mexico ($224 billion) and Taiwan ($210 billion) each top China. Play the years to watch the blue spread across Southeast Asia.

captions.201812: 2018: the deficit with China peaks at $418 billion.
captions.202412: 2024: China still accounts for a quarter of the US goods deficit.
captions.202608: China has dropped to fourth place.

scenes.title: Shifted, not shrunk
scenes.text: Compared with 2024, the deficit with China shrank by $131 billion. But the deficit with Taiwan grew by $137 billion, with Vietnam by $106 billion, Thailand by $61 billion and Mexico by $56 billion. Blue marks where the US deficit grew. By accounting, a country's trade deficit mirrors the gap between what it invests and what it saves. Unless tariffs change that gap, they mostly move the deficit from one partner to another.

scenes.title: Gold makes the gap look smaller
scenes.text: The total gap peaked at $1.38 trillion in the 12 months to March 2025, when companies rushed in goods ahead of the tariffs. In the 12 months to August 2026 it was $1.12 trillion. Imports did not fall. Exports rose, by $326 billion on 2024, the most to Switzerland, a centre of the gold trade: US gold exports more than doubled in January to August 2026, to $87 billion.
